subtitulo: Negotiating a menu with conflicting needs
descripcion: Persuasion in English leans on framing rather than force: presenting your proposal in terms of the other side's interest, offering conditional concessions, making it easy to say yes. The move that matters most is separating positions from interests — a position has one solution, an interest has several.

filas: I was thinking somewhere around X
If you could be flexible on the date, I'd be able to move on the price
What would it take for this to work for you?
converts a position into a problem
I think we want the same thing; we disagree about how
Suppose we tried it for three months and reviewed it
I can't do X, but here's what I can do
…because the alternative is another month empty

ejemplos.texto: *If you could be flexible on the date, I'd be able to move on the price.*
*What would it take for this to work for you?*
*I can't do the full amount, but I can do it in two payments this month.*
*Suppose we tried it for three months and reviewed it.*
*I think we want the same thing here; we just disagree about how.*

notas: Conditional offers concede nothing until reciprocated. That is why they are the workhorse.
*What would it take?* is the most useful negotiating question in English.
Giving a reason materially increases compliance, even a weak one. *Because* does real work.

es.en: Spanish has the same conditional language for opening positions («nuestra propuesta inicial sería…» – our starting point would be…), so the phrases transfer. What needs practice is setting an ambitious first figure and justifying it, since English treats the first offer as an anchor.
es.es: El español tiene el mismo lenguaje condicional para las posiciones iniciales («nuestra propuesta inicial sería…» – «our starting point would be…»), por lo que las expresiones se transfieren. Lo que hay que practicar es fijar una primera cifra ambiciosa y justificarla, ya que en inglés la primera oferta funciona como ancla.

de.en: «Unser Ausgangspunkt wäre…» corresponds exactly to our starting point would be…, with the same conditional. The language of anchoring therefore transfers directly.
de.de: «Unser Ausgangspunkt wäre…» entspricht genau «our starting point would be…», einschließlich des Konditionals. Die Sprache des Verhandelns und Ankerns lässt sich daher direkt übertragen.

errores: *I want* repeated — replace with *I'm looking for*, *what would help is*, *my constraint is*.
Conceding without a counter-ask, which resets expectations for the whole negotiation.
Confusing persuasion with volume or repetition.

mision.consigna: Negotiate a shared dinner plan with someone who has a *food intolerance* and someone who hates *food waste*.
requisitos: one concession that asks for something back

microtareas.texto: Write the interest behind each person's position.
Draft three *Would it help if…* proposals.
Record 90 seconds persuading someone to try a dish you had *to acquire a taste for*.

autochequeo: Did I frame in terms of their interest or mine?
Did I anchor, or open at my minimum?
Did I give a reason for each ask?
promptCorreccion: Focus only on persuasion and negotiation. (1) Check each conditional offer for unilateral concession. (2) Say whose interest I framed around. (3) Flag any concession without a counter-ask. (4) Rewrite my opening so it anchors higher without sounding unreasonable. Do not rewrite the rest.
